verses.text: “I made a covenant with my eyes. How could I look at a young woman with lust?
What share would I get from God above? What inheritance would the Almighty on high give me?
Isn’t it calamity for the unrighteous and disaster for people who do wrong?
Doesn’t he see how I live and count every step I take?
“If I’ve walked with lies and rushed into deceit,
then weigh me on honest scales so God can know my integrity.
If I’ve stepped off the right path, if my heart has chased what my eyes saw, or if any stain has stuck to my hands,
then let me plant and someone else eat. Let what grows in my field be pulled up by the roots.
“If my heart has been drawn to another woman and I’ve lain in wait at my neighbor’s door,
then let my wife grind grain for another man and let others sleep with her.
That would be a terrible crime, a wrong for the judges to punish.
It’s a fire that burns all the way to destruction and would uproot everything I’ve gained.
“If I brushed aside the complaint of a man or woman who serves me when they had a case against me,
what would I do when God rises up? When he calls me to account, what would I say?
Didn’t the same one who made me in the womb make my servant too? Didn’t one God shape us both in the womb?
“If I’ve refused the poor what they needed or let a widow’s eyes fail from waiting,
or eaten my own bit of food alone without sharing it with the fatherless,
though from my youth I’ve raised the fatherless like a father, and from my earliest days I’ve guided the widow,
if I’ve watched someone perish for lack of clothes or seen a needy person with nothing to cover them,
if their heart hasn’t blessed me because wool from my own sheep kept them warm,
if I’ve raised my hand against the fatherless because I knew I had support at the city gate,
then let my shoulder fall from its blade and my arm break off at the bone.
Disaster from God terrifies me. Before his majesty I can do nothing.
“If I’ve put my hope in gold and told fine gold, ‘You’re what I count on,’
if I’ve celebrated how rich I was and how much my own hand had gained,
if I’ve watched the sun shining or the moon moving in splendor,
and my heart got drawn in secretly and I blew them a kiss from my hand,
that too would be a wrong for the judges to punish. I’d have denied God above.
“If I’ve celebrated the downfall of someone who hated me or felt triumphant when trouble caught up with them,
though I’ve never let my mouth sin by calling down a curse on their life,
if the men of my household haven’t said, ‘Who can find anyone who hasn’t eaten their fill of his meat?’
though no foreigner had to spend the night in the street because I opened my doors to travelers,
if I’ve covered up my wrongs like Adam, hiding my guilt in my heart,
because I feared the crowd and was so scared of being looked down on by families that I kept quiet and stayed indoors,
if only I had someone who’d hear me! Look, here’s my signature! Let the Almighty answer me! Let my accuser write out the charges!
I’d carry them on my shoulder and wear them like a crown.
I’d tell him every step I took. I’d approach him like a prince.
If my land cries out against me and its furrows weep together,
if I’ve eaten what it grew without paying or caused its owners to lose their lives,
then let thorns grow instead of wheat and stinkweed instead of barley.” That’s the end of Job’s words.
